text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A winner for the biggest lottery win in Estonia of 1.3 million kroons is expected to be revealed at today's Bingo lottery session.
- The Estonian state has bought an 11 million kroon building for its embassy in Stockholm.
- Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves welcomed the statement of German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Estonia being a special case in EU expansion. Ilves leaves for visit to Sweden today.

- Prime minister Tiit Vaehi deceived his partners in the ruling coalition by rejecting a decree on minimum reference prices for imported agricultural products. Tariffs for imported agricultural goods are one of the main demands of the government coalition's rural parties.
- Tallinn spent 3.5 million kroons on the removal of snow in December and the costs are expected to be 4 million in January, officials said.
- Stickers enabling the checking of passports by machines have to be added to 900,000 Estonian passports already issued, migration officials said.
- European Union has agreed to extend until the end of 1997 the period for establishing custom tariffs in Estonia.
- Privatisation Agency council approved the list of companies that are to be privatised in 1997.
- Tallinna Pank bought 20 percent of Latvian bank Saules Bank.
- Securities inspectors are investigating rumours about high-ranking officials making profits in Union Bank share deals.
- The Kadarik firm, which owns the three largest food shops in Tallinn, is facing bankruptcy with 29 million kroons of debts.
